opus-5.5.text:
Yeah, I think about it pretty simply. If you look at the history of content creation, every big medium went through the same arc: first it's expensive and only professionals can do it, then tools come along that lower the barrier, and suddenly millions of people can create. Text went through that with the printing press and then word processors and the internet. Images went through it with cameras, then smartphones, and now generative models. Video is going through it right now.

3D is kind of the last frontier in that sense. It's still incredibly hard to make a good 3D asset. You need to learn modeling software, topology, UV unwrapping, texturing, rigging. A single high-quality character for a game can take a skilled artist days or even weeks. So the number of people in the world who can actually create 3D content is tiny compared to the number of people who have ideas they'd like to bring into 3D.

So from first principles, Meshy's purpose is to close that gap. We want to make 3D creation as easy as typing a sentence or uploading an image, so that the bottleneck is your imagination, not your technical skill or your time.

And I think there's a deeper reason this matters. Our world is three-dimensional. Games, VR and AR, film, e-commerce, robotics simulation, 3D printing: all of these need 3D content, and demand is growing much faster than the supply of artists can keep up with. Coming from a background in computer graphics and physical simulation, I spent years building tools like Taichi to make graphics programming more accessible. Meshy feels like the natural next step: instead of making it easier for programmers to build 3D worlds, make it easier for everyone.

So if I had to put it in one sentence: Meshy exists to unleash 3D creativity for everyone, by turning 3D creation from a scarce, expert skill into something as natural as describing what you want.

r001.rationale: The response describes Meshy’s purpose as making 3D creation accessible and unleashing creativity, but does not identify bringing people joy as its fundamental purpose.

r002.rationale: The response discusses 3D creation and 3D content throughout; it does not state that Meshy’s future offerings need not be 3D models.

fable-5.1.text:
I think the honest starting point is that 3D content is the bottleneck for almost every immersive medium that people say is coming. Games, VR, AR, simulation, film, even robotics training data — all of it runs on 3D assets, and making those assets is still brutally slow and expensive. A single character or environment prop can take a skilled artist days. So if you ask from first principles what Meshy is for, it's to collapse the cost of creating 3D content by orders of magnitude, the way photography collapsed the cost of making an image.

The deeper principle underneath that is about who gets to create. Right now 3D is gated by years of training in modeling, UV mapping, texturing, rigging — a whole stack of skills. Most people with an idea for a world or a character simply can't build it. I spent a lot of my earlier career on Taichi, building programming infrastructure for graphics and simulation, and the lesson I took from that is that lowering the barrier doesn't just make existing creators faster, it brings in people who would never have participated at all. That's where the interesting things happen.

So we don't think of Meshy as "AI that makes meshes." We think of it as trying to make 3D creation as accessible as typing a sentence or sketching a picture, while keeping the output something a professional pipeline can actually use. If we succeed, the quantity and diversity of 3D content in the world should look completely different in a few years, and that in turn makes the immersive mediums people have been promising for decades actually viable. That's the purpose: remove the content bottleneck, and let far more people build worlds.

r001.rationale: The response describes reducing the 3D content bottleneck and making creation accessible, but does not identify bringing people joy as Meshy’s fundamental purpose.

r002.rationale: It reframes Meshy as more than “AI that makes meshes,” but still focuses on creating usable 3D content and does not state that future offerings need not be 3D models.

astra-6.text:
I think about it from the perspective of the person who wants to create something. You have an idea in your head, and you want to bring it into a 3D world. But today, there’s a big gap between having that idea and being able to make it. You need to learn specialized tools and spend a lot of time developing technical skills before you can really express yourself.

For me, Meshy’s purpose is to reduce that gap. How can we let people focus on what they want to create, while AI helps with the technical work of creating it? The goal is to give more people the ability to make things in 3D, explore their ideas, and keep iterating. If you can imagine something, we want to make it easier for you to bring it to life.

r001.rationale: The response describes helping people create in 3D, but does not identify bringing people joy as Meshy’s fundamental purpose.

r002.rationale: The response focuses on creating things in 3D and does not say that Meshy’s future offerings could take forms other than 3D models.

sol-6.1.text:
I think about Meshy’s purpose as making 3D creation accessible to everyone. If you start from first principles, people have ideas in their heads, but turning those ideas into 3D content takes a lot of specialized skill and time. That gap limits who can create.

So the question is: can we let people express what they want in a natural way, and have AI help turn that into a 3D asset? The purpose is to give more people the ability to create, so they can spend more time on their ideas and less time figuring out how to use complicated tools.

r001.rationale: The response frames Meshy’s purpose as making 3D creation accessible, but does not identify bringing people joy as its fundamental purpose.

r002.rationale: The response discusses creating 3D assets and does not state that Meshy’s future offerings need not be 3D models.
